intents.title: Reserve only an available seat
intents.request:
### Requirement: Reserve only an available seat
Allow a reservation only when at least one seat remains.

#### Scenario: Available capacity
With two seats remaining, allow a reservation.

#### Scenario: Full event
With zero seats remaining, deny a reservation.

#### Scenario: Invalid negative capacity
With negative remaining capacity, deny a reservation.
intents.expected:
Available capacity: With two seats remaining, allow a reservation.
Full event: With zero seats remaining, deny a reservation.
Invalid negative capacity: With negative remaining capacity, deny a reservation.

result.summary: The current check allows reservations with zero seats remaining, which conflicts with the confirmed requirement.
result.purpose: Allow a reservation only when at least one seat remains; deny it when capacity is zero or negative.
result.logic: In src/reservation.js, line 2 defines canReserve(remainingSeats). Line 3 compares remainingSeats with zero using >=, meaning “greater than or equal to,” and returns true or false.
result.consequence: Reading this check: two seats returns true, as required; zero seats also returns true, contrary to the requirement; negative capacity returns false, as required. The supplied file does not show how this result is used to accept or reject an actual reservation.

steps.title: Identify the input
steps.text: remainingSeats is the capacity value passed into the function. Its source and validation are not shown.

steps.title: Examine the boundary
steps.text: The equality part of >= includes zero among the allowed values. Compare that boundary with the requirement’s phrase “at least one seat remains.”

questions: Which comparison would allow two seats while excluding both zero and negative values?
Where is canReserve called, and does a false result actually prevent a reservation?
Is remainingSeats guaranteed to be an integer, and where is it validated?
Are there tests for the three specified scenarios? No test files were supplied.
